title: Math icse GST chapter Test
description: Math icse GST chapter Test 10 question 3 marks each
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A manufacturer in Delhi sells a machine to a wholesaler in Patna for ₹50,000. The wholesaler then sells it to a dealer in Patna at a profit of ₹5,000. If the rate of GST is 18%, calculate the net GST liability of the wholesaler payable to the government.
questions.explanation: For the wholesaler, the purchase from Delhi to Patna is an inter-state transaction. Input Tax (IGST) paid = 18% of ₹50,000 = ₹9,000. The sale from Patna to Patna is an intra-state transaction. Selling Price = ₹50,000 + ₹5,000 (profit) = ₹55,000. Total Output Tax (CGST + SGST) collected = 18% of ₹55,000 = ₹9,900. Net GST Liability = Total Output Tax - Total Input Tax = ₹9,900 - ₹9,000 = ₹900.

questions.question: The printed price of an air conditioner is ₹40,000. A wholesaler gives a discount of 15% to a dealer in the same city. The dealer sells it to a consumer at the printed price. If the GST rate is 28%, find the tax paid by the dealer to the State Government.
questions.explanation: Both transactions are intra-state, so GST is shared equally between CGST (14%) and SGST (14%). Discount received by dealer = 15% of ₹40,000 = ₹6,000. Cost Price for dealer = ₹40,000 - ₹6,000 = ₹34,000. Selling Price for dealer = ₹40,000. Profit made by dealer = ₹40,000 - ₹34,000 = ₹6,000. The tax paid by the dealer to the State Government is the Net SGST, which is calculated directly on the profit. Net SGST = 14% of Profit = 14% of ₹6,000 = ₹840.

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought a television at a discount of 20% from a wholesaler. The printed price of the TV is ₹35,000. The shopkeeper sells it to a consumer at the printed price. If the sales are intra-state and the rate of GST is 12%, calculate the net CGST paid by the shopkeeper.
questions.explanation: The transactions are intra-state, so CGST is 6% and SGST is 6%. Discount received by shopkeeper = 20% of ₹35,000 = ₹7,000. This discount is also the shopkeeper's profit since they sell it at the full printed price. The net CGST liability of the shopkeeper is simply the CGST rate applied to the value added (profit). Net CGST = 6% of ₹7,000 = (6/100) × 7000 = ₹420.

questions.question: A dealer in Agra (UP) supplies goods to a dealer in Mathura (UP). The Mathura dealer supplies the same goods to a consumer in Delhi. The profit made by the Mathura dealer is ₹4,000. If the rate of GST is 18% and the IGST paid by the consumer is ₹8,100, find the original selling price of the Agra dealer.
questions.explanation: The sale from Mathura to Delhi is inter-state, meaning IGST is charged on the final selling price. IGST = 18% of the Mathura dealer's Selling Price. So, 8100 = (18/100) × SP. SP = (8100 × 100) / 18 = ₹45,000. This ₹45,000 includes the Mathura dealer's profit of ₹4,000. Therefore, the Cost Price for the Mathura dealer = ₹45,000 - ₹4,000 = ₹41,000. This cost price is exactly the selling price of the Agra dealer.

questions.question: A customer purchases the following items from a supermarket in Kanpur: Cosmetics for ₹1,500 (GST rate 18%), Stationary for ₹800 (GST rate 12%), and Clothes for ₹2,500 (GST rate 5%). Assuming all transactions are intra-state, calculate the total bill amount paid by the customer.
questions.explanation:
Calculate the total amount (Cost + GST) for each item separately.
Cosmetics: ₹1500 + 18% of 1500 = 1500 + 270 = ₹1,770.
Stationary: ₹800 + 12% of 800 = 800 + 96 = ₹896.
Clothes: ₹2500 + 5% of 2500 = 2500 + 125 = ₹2,625.
Total Bill Amount = 1770 + 896 + 2625 = ₹5,291.

questions.question: A registered computer dealer in Kolkata buys a laptop from a manufacturer in Kolkata for ₹45,000. He sells it to a consumer in Asansol (West Bengal) at a profit of ₹5,500. If the GST rate is 18%, calculate the total amount paid by the consumer.
questions.explanation: The selling price of the dealer to the consumer = Cost Price + Profit = ₹45,000 + ₹5,500 = ₹50,500. Since the sale is within West Bengal (Kolkata to Asansol), the total GST charged to the consumer is 18% of the final selling price. Total GST = 18% of ₹50,500 = ₹9,090. The total amount paid by the consumer = Selling Price + GST = ₹50,500 + ₹9,090 = ₹59,590.

questions.question: A manufacturer listed the price of a commercial oven at ₹60,000. He sells it to a wholesaler at a 20% discount. The wholesaler sells it to a retailer at a 10% discount on the listed price. If the GST is 28% and all sales are intra-state, find the Net GST paid by the wholesaler to the government.
questions.explanation: Cost Price for the wholesaler = ₹60,000 - (20% of 60,000) = ₹60,000 - ₹12,000 = ₹48,000. Selling Price of the wholesaler (sold to retailer at 10% discount on list price) = ₹60,000 - (10% of 60,000) = ₹60,000 - ₹6,000 = ₹54,000. Profit made by the wholesaler = SP - CP = ₹54,000 - ₹48,000 = ₹6,000. Net GST liability = GST% × Profit = 28% of ₹6,000 = (28/100) × 6000 = ₹1,680.

questions.question: A wholesaler in Gujarat sells an article to a dealer in Gujarat for ₹20,000. The dealer sells it to a consumer in Rajasthan at a profit of 25%. If the rate of GST is 12%, calculate the net IGST paid by the dealer to the Central Government.
questions.explanation: The first transaction is intra-state (Gujarat to Gujarat), so the dealer pays Input CGST = 6% of 20000 = ₹1200 and Input SGST = 6% of 20000 = ₹1200. Total Input Tax = ₹2,400. The second transaction is inter-state (Gujarat to Rajasthan). Selling Price = ₹20,000 + 25% profit = ₹25,000. Output IGST = 12% of ₹25,000 = ₹3,000. Net IGST liability = Output IGST - Total Input Tax (Input CGST + Input SGST can be set off against IGST) = ₹3,000 - ₹2,400 = ₹600.

questions.question: The printed price of an article is ₹50,000. A wholesaler allows a discount of 10% to a shopkeeper. The shopkeeper sells it to a consumer at 4% above the printed price. If the applicable GST rate is 18%, find the profit earned by the shopkeeper.
questions.explanation: Cost Price for the shopkeeper = Printed Price - 10% Discount = ₹50,000 - ₹5,000 = ₹45,000. The shopkeeper sells the article at 4% above the printed price. Selling Price = ₹50,000 + (4% of 50,000) = ₹50,000 + ₹2,000 = ₹52,000. The profit earned is simply Selling Price minus Cost Price (tax is not part of the core profit calculation). Profit = ₹52,000 - ₹45,000 = ₹7,000.

questions.question: The printed price of an article is ₹30,000. A dealer in Delhi buys it at a 20% discount from a wholesaler in Delhi. The dealer sells it to a consumer in Haryana at a discount of 10% on the printed price. The GST rate is 12%. Find the Net GST liability of the dealer.
questions.explanation: For the intra-state purchase (Delhi to Delhi): Cost Price = ₹30,000 - 20% = ₹24,000. Input Tax = 12% of ₹24,000 = ₹2,880 (which is ₹1,440 CGST and ₹1,440 SGST). For the inter-state sale (Delhi to Haryana): Selling Price = ₹30,000 - 10% = ₹27,000. Output IGST = 12% of ₹27,000 = ₹3,240. The Net GST liability = Output Tax - Input Tax = ₹3,240 - ₹2,880 = ₹360.
